297	### SFCC-270 — Cart Item UI Part 1 · 9 ACs · all buildable
298	
299	ACs: per line item — image; name to the right of the image; price; selected colour; selected size;
300	quantity with `+`/`–` either side; multiple items each individually identifiable; Remove and Wishlist
301	as **underlined text links below the stepper**; on mobile nothing truncated or hidden.
302	
303	**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-16): override base `product-item`.** Cart keeps using it. Separately,
304	upcoming wishlist work moves the account wishlist page onto `ZimmProductCard` (which already has a
305	`variation: 'wishlist'` with `showRemove`), so it stops consuming `product-item` at that point.
306	
307	Accurate consumer map — **two chains only**:
308	```
309	pages/cart  ->  components/product-item-list  ->  components/product-item
310	pages/account/wishlist  ->  components/product-item          (direct)
311	```
312	Checkout does **not** use it. The base has two separate line-item systems: `product-item` (the full
313	interactive row) and `item-variant/*` (a read-only composition used by `order-summary`, i.e. the
314	checkout summaries).
315	
316	**Copy-first scope — 3 files** from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item/`:
317	`index.jsx` (7.4 KB), `bonus-product-quantity.jsx` (1.5 KB), `product-quantity-picker.jsx` (3.4 KB),
318	each to `.tsx`. Base's own `.test.js`/`.test.jsx` are not copied — write our own.
319	
320	**The finding that changes the size of the job:** `product-item/index.jsx` renders its visible content
321	through **five more base components** — `components/item-variant` plus `item-variant/item-image`,
322	`item-name`, `item-attributes`, `item-price`. So overriding `product-item` gives you the row's
323	*structure and controls*; the *content pieces* still come from `item-variant/*`. Styling those to
324	Figma means either overriding `item-variant/*` too — which also changes `order-summary`, and
325	therefore the checkout summaries — or not using them inside our override and composing the content
326	ourselves. **Decide this before starting: it is the difference between a 3-file override and an
327	8-file one with checkout blast radius.**
328	
329	**`shared/ui` barrel trap applies.** `product-item/index.jsx` imports from `components/shared/ui`.
330	Per the known trap, overriding an individual `shared/ui/<Name>` intercepts nothing — 208 base files
331	import the barrel, so only overriding the barrel itself has any effect.
332	
333	**Bridge-pattern requirement:** because `product-item` is used internally by base components, the
334	override's **default export must stay API-compatible** (full original prop surface) so
335	`product-item-list` and the wishlist page keep working. Per `overrideStyling.md`, put brand styling
336	in a **theme recipe**, not a named-export split — token-driven theming doesn't need the second
337	export that `CardBaseline`'s prop-narrowing did.
338	
339	**DECIDED (Marcel, 2026-09-16): Option B — override `item-variant/*` as well. 8 files.**
340	`product-item/{index,bonus-product-quantity,product-quantity-picker}` +
341	`item-variant/{index,item-image,item-name,item-attributes,item-price}`, all to `.tsx`.
342	
343	Verified before deciding: **every consumer of `item-variant/*` is base/OOTB with no Zimmermann
344	design or development**, so brand styling landing on them is an upgrade toward Zimmermann, not a
345	regression from it. Full consumer list — `components/order-summary` (no override),
346	`components/multiship/multiship-order-summary`, `pages/account/order-detail` (account has zero
347	overrides), `pages/account/wishlist/partials/wishlist-primary-action` +
348	`wishlist-secondary-button-group` (and wishlist is migrating to `ZimmProductCard` anyway),
349	`pages/cart/partials/cart-secondary-button-group` (base cart page, replaced by the drawer),
350	`pages/checkout/partials/{pickup-address,product-shipping-address-card,shipping-product-cards}`
351	(checkout override is only `payment.tsx`), `pages/checkout-one-click/partials/one-click-product-shipping-address-card`.
352	
353	**`pages/confirmation` is NOT in the blast radius** — `overrides/app/pages/confirmation/index.tsx`
354	already exists and does not use `item-variant`, so the base confirmation page is shadowed and never
355	renders. That was the one surface worth worrying about (a shopper sees it after paying).
356	
357	**Two requirements for the override, both load-bearing:**
358	1. **Keep the defaults-then-spread order.** Callers set their own geometry —
359	   `order-summary` does `<CartItemVariantImage width="80px" mr={2} />` — and must keep winning.
360	   Write `<Box width={zimmDefault} {...props}>`, never the reverse, or you break layouts that work
361	   today. `item-image`, `item-attributes` and `item-price` already have it right.
362	2. **Fix `item-name` while in there.** Base is `<Link {...props} color="black.600">` — spread
363	   *before* the colour, so no caller can ever override it. Move the spread after; no base caller
364	   passes `color`, so nothing changes for them.
365	
366	**Deferred consequence, accepted:** when checkout is designed it will inherit cart-derived
367	line-item styling it never specified. Whoever picks up checkout should know why it already looks
368	part-branded.
369	
370	**Governance:** `overrides/app/components/product-item/` is **Tier 2, Squad B-owned (notify Squad A)**
371	per `protectedFiles.md`. CODEOWNERS will request Squad B's review on a Squad A ticket.
372	
373	**Interim consequence, low risk:** while the account wishlist page still consumes `product-item`, our
374	override's styling reaches it too. `overrides/app/pages/` contains no account pages at all — account
375	is entirely base and unstyled today — so the exposure is minimal until the wishlist migration lands.
376

7. **`'ZimmCartItemVariant'`**, duplicated verbatim at `item-image.tsx:47`, `item-attributes.tsx:52`, `item-price.tsx:41` — extract to one shared constant.

Side with the Orchestrator against the Tester here.

`overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts:142-143` — the comment directly above `caption` labels it `// Default/Caption`, but the value it assigns is medium-weight, i.e. what Figma actually calls `Caption-strong`.
